title: Transient Privilege Sanctuary and Evidence Handoff
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines the Transient Privilege Sanctuary (TPS) pattern: a controlled, timeboxed environment used to grant elevated access for emergency operations, sensitive debugging, and incident remediation. TPS centralizes high-privilege activity into a monitored ‘sanctuary’ that simplifies evidence capture, reduces blast radius, and ensures a deterministic handoff of forensic artifacts to the Incident Response (IR) and Compliance teams.

Intended audience
-----------------
- Incident responders and on-call engineers
- Platform and SRE teams
- Security and compliance reviewers
- Engineering managers responsible for high-privilege operations

Scope and applicability
----------------------
This procedure applies to all scenarios where temporary elevation of access is required for:
1) emergency production fixes (SEV2+/SEV1)
2) on-demand root-level debugging for customer-impacting incidents
3) forensics that require short-lived access to encrypted model artifacts or tenant data

It does NOT replace long-term privileged accounts, break-glass procedures for legal hold with counsel, or dedicated cross-tenant escalations that must follow separate contractual workflows.

Definitions
-----------
- Transient Privilege Sanctuary (TPS): an isolated execution context (K8s namespace or dedicated bastion instance) provisioned for short-lived privileged tasks with enhanced telemetry and evidence packaging.
- Sanctuary Token: a cryptographically bound token issued by the Privilege Broker that enforces TTL and usage constraints.
- Privilege Broker: service that authorizes TPS sessions, records policy decisions, and emits audit records to the canonical audit stream.
- Evidence Hand-Off Bundle (EHB): a signed, time-stamped package of logs, session transcripts, artifacts, and provenance metadata delivered to IR/compliance.

Design principles
-----------------
- Minimize scope: TPS sessions grant only the minimum entitlement for the task.
- Immutable provenance: all TPS activity is captured with tamper-evident signatures and cryptographic timestamps.
- Deterministic retention: EHBs follow a retention schedule that meets regulatory and contractual SLAs.
- Rapid revocation: sanctuary tokens can be revoked immediately via the Privilege Broker and must cascade to active sessions within 5s.

High-level workflow
-------------------
1. Request: Pager/SEV owner requests TPS access via the IR runbook UI (or CLI) with justification and TTL (max 4 hours).
2. Authorization: Privilege Broker evaluates policy (RBAC + risk signals) and issues a Sanctuary Token with embedded constraints.
3. Provision: TPS environment instantiated (pre-warmed sandbox namespace/bastion) and token-bound session created.
4. Observe: Enhanced telemetry captures session recording, keystroke-level transcript, system-level audit logs, and network flow traces.
5. Action: Operator performs remediation tasks.
6. Terminate: Session ends either on TTL expiry, manual termination, or forced revocation after escalation.
7. Package & Handoff: Evidence Hand-Off Bundle (EHB) automatically assembled and signed; delivered to IR and Compliance repositories.

Detailed procedures
-------------------
Requesting TPS access
1. Initiate from the incident runbook UI: select incident ID, attach justification (concise), and propose TTL.
2. If UI unavailable, use CLI: 
   - cli: rdx tps request --incident=INC-12345 --reason="memory-corruption-debug" --ttl=2h --approver=oncall@team.com
3. Approval is automated for pre-authorized roles; otherwise, a 2-minute interactive approval is required from the incident commander.

Privilege Broker policy checks
- RBAC: evaluate role bindings (source-of-truth: Entitlement Service) and require at least two attributes: requester_role and incident_severity.
- Risk signals: ongoing active breaches, anomalous high-rate requests by the requester, or external vendor constraints will block issuance.
- Data residency checks: if requested artifacts span geo-fenced data, TPS must be instantiated in the permitted region or be denied.

Provisioning checklist (pre-provisioned sandbox images recommended)
- Ensure TPM-backed host keys and ephemeral filesystem mount with encryption-at-rest (AES-256).
- Inject only required secrets via short-lived KMS grants (max duration: session TTL).
- Network ACLs: restrict egress to monitoring collectors and internal control plane endpoints.
- Observability hooks: session recording (ffmpeg-style), keystroke capture, syscall auditing (auditd or eBPF), and packet capture for targeted flows.

Runtime telemetry and mandatory audit fields
- TPS session start/end timestamps (RFC3339).
- Sanctuary Token ID and issuing policy hash.
- Requester identity (OIDC sub) and role assertion.
- Action transcripts (base64-encoded) and session recording reference URI (signed).
- Resource scope list (ARNs or internal IDs) and changed file manifests (SHA256).
- Network flows with 5-tuples, direction, and bytes transferred.

Example audit JSON (canonical event)
{
  "event_type": "tps.session",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-15T14:22:05Z",
  "session_id": "tps-9f2b3a",
  "token_id": "st-7c3d2f",
  "requester": "alice@example.com",
  "policy_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "scope": ["svc/model-store:read","k8s/namespace:exec"],
  "transcript_uri": "s3://ir-evidence/tps/tps-9f2b3a/transcript.gz",
  "recording_uri": "s3://ir-evidence/tps/tps-9f2b3a/session.mp4",
  "signatures": {"broker": "sig-v1:...","collector":"sig-v1:..."}
}

Note: the canonical audit stream must also include the event signature metadata and an HMAC over the payload forwarded to the immutable audit store.

Evidence Hand-Off Bundle (EHB) composition
- manifest.json (signed) with provenance fields
- raw session recording (mp4/ogg)
- terminal transcript (gzip, base64)
- exported kernel traces (if enabled)
- list of modified artifacts with SHA256 and backup copies
- privilege broker decision log slice
- retention policy tag and TTL

EHB packaging sample command
- rdx tps package --session=tps-9f2b3a --output=s3://ir-evidence/tps/tps-9f2b3a/ehb.tar.gz

Retention and access controls for EHBs
- Default retention: 540 days (production incidents) unless legal hold applies.
- Access policy: IR and Compliance roles only; access requests must be tracked via Access Request Service and produce an access-audit event.
- Shorter retention for non-sensitive artefacts: 90 days for ephemeral infra-only sessions (flagged in manifest).
- Tamper-evidence: every EHB is signed by the Privilege Broker key and stored in an immutable bucket with WORM enabled.

Escalation and rollback
- Immediate revocation: on detection of misuse or compromise, Security may call the Privilege Broker revoke endpoint: 
  - curl -X POST https://priv-broker.internal/revoke -d '{"token_id":"st-7c3d2f"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SEC_API_KEY'
- If session cannot be revoked (network partition), initiate emergency containment: snapshot affected instances, isolate network, and follow forensics runbook.
- Notification: Revocation produces a high-priority IR ticket; all active sessions are enumerated and EHB pre-assembly begins.

Testing and game days
- Quarterly game days: simulate TPS provisioning and EHB handoff using a synthetic incident.
- KPIs: time-to-provision (goal < 90s), time-to-revoke (goal < 5s), EHB assembly completion (goal < 3 min after session termination).

Operational metrics to monitor
- TPS issuance rate (per team and per user)
- Average session duration and TTL usage distribution
- EHB generation success rate and packaging latency
- Number of revocations and post-revocation anomalies detected

Ownership and responsibilities
- Security (owner): maintain Privilege Broker, define policy rules, rotate broker keys quarterly, and approve EHB retention exceptions.
- SRE/Platform: maintain TPS sandbox images, observability collectors, and ensure revocation signals propagate.
- Incident Commander: approve ad-hoc TPS sessions when automated checks block issuance.
- Compliance: validate EHBs for regulatory discovery and provide retention guidance for contractual customers.

Compliance mapping and evidence use-cases
- SOC2 / ISO27001: EHBs provide objective evidence for privileged access and operations during audits.
- Data residency: TPS must respect geo-fencing; EHB metadata records residency boundaries and storage region.
- Legal hold: when flagged by Legal, EHB retention is extended and WORM locks applied.

Appendix A: RBAC policy snippet (YAML)
apiVersion: rdx/v1
kind: PrivilegePolicy
metadata:
  name: tps-emergency-policy
rules:
  - role: sevreponder
    allow:
      - action: tps:request
      - action: tps:execute
    constraints:
      ttl_max: 4h
      require_2fa: true

Appendix B: Minimal forensic checklist for IR
- Ensure EHB signature valid and timestamped.
- Validate session transcript against recording (integrity).
- Snapshot any modified artifacts and compute checksums.
- Correlate network flows with observability traces.
- Produce preliminary timeline and attach to incident ticket.
